html:
Benazir Bhutto was twice prime minister of Pakistan, from 1988 to 1990 and from 1993 to 1996. She was the first woman elected to lead a Muslim majority country in modern times.

Born in Karachi in 1953, she was the daughter of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, founder of the Pakistan Peoples Party and prime minister in the 1970s. She studied at Harvard and Oxford. In 1977 General Zia ul Haq overthrew her father, and in 1979 had him hanged. She spent years in prison, under house arrest and in exile while leading the party.

After Zia died in a plane crash in 1988, she won the election at 35. Both her governments were dismissed by the president on charges of corruption and misrule, and her husband, Asif Ali Zardari, was jailed for years. She went into exile again in 1998.

She came home in October 2007 to run in new elections and survived a bomb attack on her return. On 27 December 2007 she was killed by a gunman and suicide bomber after a rally in Rawalpindi. Her husband later became president.
